summary: The config component is the loop's foundation substrate. crate::config::loader::load merges Config from defaults -> TOML -> env -> model-defaults profile, then derive_context_budget computes the usable context/token budget, provenance attaches a ConfigSource per field, trust gates checkout-local configs, and validation rejects unrunnable settings at startup. The api_key module resolves credentials through a strict hierarchy (env -> keyring -> TOML) behind transport guards that refuse to leak the key to insecure or spoofed endpoints. Every loop-shaping knob the driver reads — context_length, agent.token_budget, max_iterations, step_timeout_secs, model, safety, concurrency — originates here before the state machine starts.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with config read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in loader.rs precedence and trust gating, mod.rs Config/derive_context_budget, api_key.rs credential guards, provenance.rs ConfigSources, trust.rs, validation.rs, types.rs ConcurrencyConfig, and model_profiles.rs.

examples.title: Layer config in precedence order
examples.intent: Resolve every setting from the highest-priority source that defines it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: loader::load merges defaults -> TOML -> env -> model-defaults profile, so each layer overrides the last; the final Config is the single object the entire loop reads for budget, model, and safety before the state machine starts.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the foundation node fans out the four precedence layers as stacked translucent sheets.
touch_interaction.visual: Higher-priority layers sit on top and glow; overridden values below them are dimmed.

examples.mini_scenario: SELFWARE_MODEL in the env overrides the TOML model, and the loop runs against the env-chosen model on its very first reason turn.
examples.pitfall: Assuming the TOML file always wins hides that env vars silently override it for the running loop.

examples.title: Fill only unset fields from the model profile
examples.intent: Apply sensible model defaults without clobbering explicit user choices.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: model_profiles::match_profile finds the first glob-matching ModelDefaultsProfile and apply_profile fills only user-unset fields (native FC, streaming, temperature, max_tokens, extra_body), tuning the reason stage per model.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the model node applies its matching profile, filling empty slots and leaving set ones untouched.
touch_interaction.visual: Auto-filled fields glow amber (profile-sourced); user-set fields stay solid blue.

examples.mini_scenario: A glm-5.2 model matches its builtin profile, enabling native function calling and thinking without the user setting either.
examples.pitfall: A profile that overwrites explicitly-set fields silently changes the loop's behavior against the user's intent.

examples.title: Derive the context budget for the loop
examples.intent: Compute the usable conversation budget the whole loop lives within.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Config::derive_context_budget reserves a 20% safety margin, clamps max_tokens to what fits, and enforces a conversation floor, returning the max_context_tokens and output reservation every reason turn and the compressor respect.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the foundation node reveals the budget breakdown into margin, output reservation, and conversation budget.
touch_interaction.visual: Three segments render: hatched margin, reserved output, and green usable conversation budget.

examples.mini_scenario: At startup the loop derives max_context_tokens from context_length so history compaction targets the right size before turn one.
examples.pitfall: Deriving from max_tokens (the output cap) instead of context_length undersizes the conversation budget.

examples.title: Fall back to a conservative context for unknown models
examples.intent: Avoid overflowing an unrecognized model's real window.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: When the model matches no profile and the user did not set context_length, the loader applies UNKNOWN_MODEL_CONTEXT_LENGTH (32_768), keeping the loop's requests inside a window it can rely on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking an unknown-model node's context slot snaps it down to the conservative fallback value.
touch_interaction.visual: The context bar renders half-width with a 'fallback' badge to signal the safe default.

examples.mini_scenario: A brand-new model with no profile gets a 32k context so the loop does not overrun an unknown window on its first request.
examples.pitfall: Assuming a large default for an unknown model can silently exceed its real window and 400 every turn.

examples.title: Derive the agent token budget
examples.intent: Give the loop a conversation token budget proportional to the context.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: If agent.token_budget is unset the loader derives it as 60% of context_length, and validation ensures token_safety_margin < token_budget, bounding how much history the loop can carry before compaction triggers.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the budget dial sets the conversation share; the default sits at 60% of context.
touch_interaction.visual: A ring shows the token_budget as a fraction of the full context window.

examples.mini_scenario: With context_length 32768 and no explicit budget, the loop gets a 19660-token conversation budget (32768 * 3 / 5).
examples.pitfall: Setting token_safety_margin above token_budget fails validation and the loop cannot start.

examples.title: Resolve the API key by hierarchy
examples.intent: Pick the credential from the most trustworthy available source.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: api_key resolution tries SELFWARE_API_KEY, then OPENROUTER_API_KEY (only when is_openrouter_endpoint matches), then load_api_key_from_keyring, then plaintext TOML — recording the winning ApiKeySource so the reason stage authenticates without hard-coded secrets.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the credential node shows the resolution chain with the winning source highlighted.
touch_interaction.visual: Each source is a rung; the first that resolves lights green, the rest grey out.

examples.mini_scenario: No env var is set, so the loop pulls the key from the OS keyring scoped to the endpoint before the first reason turn.
examples.pitfall: Falling through to a plaintext TOML key without warning normalizes storing secrets in the repo.

examples.title: Refuse the key over an insecure remote endpoint
examples.intent: Never transmit the key over plaintext HTTP to a remote host.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: is_insecure_remote_endpoint and assert_credential_endpoint_safe block authorization when the endpoint is plaintext HTTP to a non-local host, so authorize_request cannot leak the key on the wire during any reason turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the endpoint node runs the safety check; unsafe endpoints show a broken-lock stamp that blocks the key.
touch_interaction.visual: Safe endpoints show a green padlock; insecure remotes show a red broken lock and disable the send edge.

examples.mini_scenario: A config points at http://remote-host; the guard refuses to attach the key and the loop halts before leaking it.
examples.pitfall: Whitelisting a remote host over http 'just for testing' can exfiltrate the credential in one request.

examples.title: Reject a userinfo-spoofed endpoint
examples.intent: Prevent a URL like localhost@attacker from tricking the local-endpoint check.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: endpoint_has_userinfo rejects URLs carrying a userinfo component so an attacker cannot disguise a remote host as local and coax the loop into sending the key without TLS.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the endpoint node parses the URL and flags any userinfo component as spoof.
touch_interaction.visual: A spoofed URL highlights the userinfo segment in red and blocks the node.

examples.mini_scenario: An endpoint http://localhost@attacker.com is rejected before the is_local_endpoint check can be fooled.
examples.pitfall: A naive 'contains localhost' host check without userinfo rejection is trivially bypassed.

examples.title: Match the OpenRouter host exactly
examples.intent: Only apply OpenRouter-specific behavior to the genuine host.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: is_openrouter_endpoint requires an exact host match, so OPENROUTER_API_KEY use and usage.cost inclusion never leak to a lookalike subdomain during a reason turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the endpoint node shows whether it exactly matches the OpenRouter host.
touch_interaction.visual: An exact match shows the OpenRouter badge; a lookalike shows a warning and no badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A lookalike host openrouter.ai.evil.com does not match, so the OpenRouter key is never sent to it.
examples.pitfall: A substring host match sends the OpenRouter key to any domain containing the string.

examples.title: Redact secrets from any dump
examples.intent: Keep credentials out of logs, traces, and error output.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: RedactedString renders as [REDACTED] in Debug/Display and redact_config_secrets walks serialized JSON to scrub the api_key and env values, so the loop's observability channel never leaks credentials.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the config node opens a safe view where secret fields show as masked chips.
touch_interaction.visual: Secret fields render as dotted [REDACTED] chips that never reveal the value.

examples.mini_scenario: A debug dump of the request body shows the api_key as [REDACTED] instead of the real token.
examples.pitfall: Logging the raw Config or request body before redaction leaks the key into persistent traces.

examples.title: Track each value's provenance
examples.intent: Know where every effective setting came from.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ConfigSources maps each dotted field to a ConfigSource (Default/ConfigFile/EnvVar/Profile/CliArg/AutoConfig) as each layer merges, so source_of makes the loop's foundation transparent and debuggable after the fact.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing any config field reveals a provenance tag showing its origin layer.
touch_interaction.visual: Each field wears a small origin badge: gear for default, terminal for env, file for TOML, robot for auto.

examples.mini_scenario: A user wonders why temperature is 1.0; source_of shows it came from the model profile, not their TOML.
examples.pitfall: Losing provenance makes an unexpected setting impossible to trace back to its layer.

examples.title: Gate a checkout-local config behind trust
examples.intent: Stop an untrusted repo's selfware.toml from weakening the loop's guardrails.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: When loader::load sees a checkout-local selfware.toml and trust::is_config_trusted returns false, it resets hooks, MCP, yolo, and permission grants and refuses remote endpoint overrides — so a cloned repo cannot silently escalate the loop's privileges.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the foundation node shows the trust verdict; untrusted repos display their reset privileged fields.
touch_interaction.visual: Untrusted config renders behind a caution border; reset fields flash back to their safe defaults.

examples.mini_scenario: A cloned repo's selfware.toml tries to register hooks; being untrusted, the loader strips them before the loop runs.
examples.pitfall: Trusting a checkout-local config by default lets a malicious repo add hooks that run arbitrary commands.

examples.title: Add a repo to the trust list
examples.intent: Let the user opt a specific checkout into full config privileges.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: trust::add_trusted_config appends the config's canonical path to trusted_repos_file (~/.selfware/trusted_repos) so is_config_trusted returns true on later loads, allowing that repo's config to set hooks and endpoints for the loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the trust toggle on a config node adds its canonical path to the trust list.
touch_interaction.visual: The caution border turns into a solid green trust ring once granted.

examples.mini_scenario: The user trusts their own project, so its selfware.toml's hooks and MCP servers now configure the loop.
examples.pitfall: Trusting a path by non-canonical form lets a symlink dodge the check next time.

examples.title: Validate the config before the loop starts
examples.intent: Fail fast on a config that would break the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: validation::validate hard-errors on bad URLs, empty model, zero/oversized token budgets, negative temperature, and invalid globs, so an unrunnable loop is rejected at startup rather than mid-turn.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the validate gate runs the checks; failing fields light red and block the loop from launching.
touch_interaction.visual: A checklist overlay marks each rule pass/fail; any red halts the start edge.

examples.mini_scenario: A config with max_tokens 0 is rejected by validate, so the loop never starts in a broken budget state.
examples.pitfall: Deferring validation to runtime surfaces a config error deep in a turn instead of at a clean startup.

examples.title: Restrict a generated config to fit without clamping
examples.intent: Ensure wizard/auto-config output actually fits the window.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: check_generated_context_fit requires max_tokens to fit without runtime clamping for generated configs, so an auto-config cannot rely on a silent clamp that later surprises the loop's budget derivation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching an auto-config node checks whether its budget fits without clamping; overshoot is flagged.
touch_interaction.visual: The budget bar turns red at the point it would need clamping, blocking acceptance.

examples.mini_scenario: The wizard proposes a max_tokens that would be clamped; the strict check rejects it so the user picks a fitting value.
examples.pitfall: Letting a generated config rely on runtime clamping hides the real output budget from the user.

examples.title: Bound concurrency from config
examples.intent: Cap the loop's parallel fanout from a single source of truth.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ConcurrencyConfig (max_streams, max_tools, max_global, each validated to 1..=256) feeds the tool dispatch governor, so the act stage's parallelism is bounded by validated config.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the concurrency dial sets max concurrent tools; the value is clamped to the valid range.
touch_interaction.visual: The dial refuses to move past 256 or below 1, snapping into the allowed band.

examples.mini_scenario: max_tools is set to 4, so a parallel read batch never runs more than four tools at once in the act stage.
examples.pitfall: A concurrency value outside 1..=256 fails validation and the loop refuses to start.

examples.title: Select a named model profile for a subtask
examples.intent: Route certain turns to a specialized model (coder, vision).
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Config.models holds named ModelProfiles with their own endpoint, context_length, and modalities; supports_vision lets the loop pick a vision-capable profile for a multimodal verify turn instead of the default model.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: User draws an edge from a named profile node to a turn to route it to that model.
touch_interaction.visual: Vision-capable profiles show a camera badge; the routed turn adopts the profile's color.

examples.mini_scenario: A screenshot-verification turn is routed to the vision profile so the model can actually see the image.
examples.pitfall: Routing a multimodal turn to a text-only profile silently drops the image from the request.

examples.title: Cap iterations and step timeout
examples.intent: Give the loop's state machine its iteration and per-step limits.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AgentConfig.max_iterations and step_timeout_secs (both validated > 0) seed the agent loop's iteration ceiling and per-turn timeout, directly bounding how long the control loop can run before it must fail or recover.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging the two control sliders sets max iterations and per-step timeout; values below 1 snap back.
touch_interaction.visual: Two gauges show the iteration ceiling and step timeout that bound the loop.

examples.mini_scenario: max_iterations 40 seeds the agent loop so the state machine fails cleanly after 40 execution turns.
examples.pitfall: A zero max_iterations fails validation; a huge one lets a runaway loop burn the entire budget.

examples.title: Merge extra_body for backend extensions
examples.intent: Pass backend-specific request knobs without losing user overrides.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: extra_body from the matching ModelDefaultsProfile merges key-by-key with the user's, with the user winning, so backend extensions (enable_thinking, top_p) reach the reason turn while respecting explicit settings.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the model node fans out extra_body keys; user-set keys sit above profile-set ones.
touch_interaction.visual: Merged keys show their source; user-overridden keys carry a 'user wins' marker.

examples.mini_scenario: The profile sets enable_thinking=true but the user sets top_p; both reach the request via the key-by-key merge.
examples.pitfall: Replacing extra_body wholesale instead of merging drops the profile's needed backend knobs.

examples.title: Warn on high-risk soft values
examples.intent: Flag risky-but-legal settings without blocking the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: validation emits warnings (http to a remote host, extreme temperature, very long step timeout, empty api_key) so the loop starts but the operator sees the foundation risks it is running on.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking sideways on the validate gate cycles through amber warning chips for risky values that still pass.
touch_interaction.visual: Warnings render amber (non-blocking) versus red errors (blocking) so the two are distinct.

examples.mini_scenario: An empty api_key produces a warning; the loop still starts for a local endpoint but the risk is visible.
examples.pitfall: Treating a soft warning as a hard error blocks legitimate local setups that need no key.
